Heard learned counsel for the petitioners as well as learned APP for the State.

2. At the outset, learned counsel for the petitioners submit that during pendency of this petition,
petitioner no. 2 has been arrested and as such, the application as against him has become infructuous.

He, therefore, seeks permission to withdraw this petition with respect to petitioner no.
2, namely, Alok Kumar.
3.
Accordingly, this petition is dismissed as withdrawn as having become infructuous with respect to petitioner no. 2.

sentences.text:
So far as the petitioner no. 1 is concerned, apprehends his arrest in connection with Sakra P.S.
Case No. 151 of 2023, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 376(D), 120(B), 506 of the I.P.C. and section 67(A) of the I.T. Act.
5.
As per allegation, petitioner no. 1 and other co- accused persons are alleged to have threatened the victim and also told her to make video viral.
The main allegation is on co- accused Sanjeev Kumar who forcibly established physical relationship with the victim and due to this act, victim got pregnant.
6. The learned counsel for the petitioner no. 1 has submitted that the petitioner is innocent and are person of clean antecedent.
Petitioner no. 1 is father of Sonal Kumar (petitioner no. 2).
The victim in her statement recorded u/s 164 Cr.P.C. has stated categorically that she had already solemnized marriage with the boy to whom she had love and affection.
She has further stated that her mother and father has falsely implicated the innocent persons in this case.
There is general and omnibus allegation against the petitioner no. 1 7.

On the other hand, the learned APP for the State and learned counsel for the counsel for the informant have Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.35178 of 2025(5) dt.02-12-2025 vehemently opposed the submission of learned counsel for the petitioner no. 1.
8.

(Nawneet Kumar Pandey, J) Ranjeet/-
